selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What question is raised at the start of the passage about all created things?
questions.answer: It asks whether all beings, in their own created way, say “In the Name of Allah.”

questions.question: What answer is given to that question?
questions.answer: A strong confirmation is given that it is true.

questions.question: What lesson do trees teach in this passage?
questions.answer: They show that they receive their provisions from Allah’s mercy and then bring fruits and benefits to people.

questions.question: What do small seeds teach us when they grow into large trees?
questions.answer: They teach us that great results can come from tiny things only through Allah’s command.

questions.question: Why are milk-giving animals called blessed in this passage?
questions.answer: Because they provide a clean and valuable food as a mercy from Allah.

questions.question: What main point is made by saying everything becomes obedient when Allah’s name is mentioned?
questions.answer: The point is that created things submit to Allah’s command.

questions.question: What makes the movement of roots through rock so meaningful?
questions.answer: Their softness makes it clear that their success does not come from brute force.

questions.question: What do the leaves show by staying moist in severe heat?
questions.answer: They show that heat does not act independently and that Allah preserves what He wills.

questions.question: What overall message do roots and leaves together give?
questions.answer: They show that both strong barriers and harsh conditions are under Allah’s control.

questions.question: What claim from earlier is confirmed at the beginning of this passage?
questions.answer: The claim that all beings say “In the Name of Allah” through their condition and actions.

questions.question: What simple real-life comparison is used to explain this idea?
questions.answer: A comparison about one man forcing the people of a town to gather and labor.

questions.question: What do trees do for people after receiving from Allah’s mercy?
questions.answer: They present fruits and other benefits to people.

questions.question: What picture is used for gardens, and what does it show?
questions.answer: Gardens are pictured like cooking pots or kitchens, showing rich and varied provision.

questions.question: What is special about the milk from the animals named in the passage?
questions.answer: It is pure, beneficial, and generously provided through Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What contrast is made between the softness of roots and the hardness of the earth?
questions.answer: The roots are very soft, but they still pass through hard ground and rock.

questions.question: What happens to the idea that nature acts by itself when we look at these examples?
questions.answer: That idea becomes weak, because the examples point beyond nature to Allah’s will.

questions.question: How does the example connected to Musa, peace be upon him, strengthen the argument?
questions.answer: It reminds the reader that Allah can make solid rock open.

questions.question: What big truth should a student understand from the final examples in the passage?
questions.answer: Even the strongest natural forces obey Allah, and delicate things succeed by His will.

questions.question: At the opening of the passage, what issue is being asked and answered?
questions.answer: Whether all beings truly declare Allah’s name through the way they are made and the way they act.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the work of trees?
questions.answer: They receive gifts from Allah’s mercy and then pass those gifts on to people.

questions.question: Which animals are mentioned, and what do they provide?
questions.answer: Cows, camels, sheep, and goats are mentioned, and they provide milk.

questions.question: How are gardens described in a way that highlights abundance?
questions.answer: They are described like places where many kinds of foods are prepared together.

questions.question: What happens to things when Allah’s name and mercy are mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: They become obedient and manageable under His command.

questions.question: What is the short question asked at the start of this passage section?
questions.answer: It asks if it is really true that all beings say “In the Name of Allah” through their condition.
